definitions.explanation: The traditional, unsimplified forms of Chinese characters, still used in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau. These are the original complex forms from which simplified characters were derived.

examples.japanese: {台湾|たいわん}では{繁体字|はんたいじ}が{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: Traditional characters are used in Taiwan.

examples.japanese: {繁体字|はんたいじ}は{画数|かくすう}が{多|おお}くて{書|か}くのが{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Traditional characters have many strokes and are difficult to write.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{漢字|かんじ}は{繁体字|はんたいじ}に{近|ちか}いものが{多|おお}いが、{独自|どくじ}の{略字|りゃくじ}もある。
examples.english: Many Japanese kanji are close to traditional characters, but there are also uniquely simplified forms.

notes:
USAGE:
Also called {正体字|せいたいじ} (standard-form characters) in Taiwan. Japanese kanji overlap significantly with traditional characters but are not identical — Japan carried out its own simplification reforms after World War II.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {繁体字|はんたいじ}で{書|か}く: to write in traditional characters
- {繁体字|はんたいじ}{圏|けん}: traditional character regions
- {繁体字|はんたいじ}{表記|ひょうき}: traditional character notation
